flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: This is the Rat's second pawn, the Small Center. I am locking e5/d5 and staying compact, not 'controlling more squares' like e4 and d4 already said. Thirty-nine centipawns of 'best' with the same center-control sticker as ply 1 teaches me the opening name is a lie.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No because-clause on the three-pawn center. f4 is the Austrian-Attack idea: space, e5 clamp, kingside storm. The dump's only tag is backward_pawn, a problem leftover that never even made the sentence. I needed 'you build a big pawn center,' not a verdict toast.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to d7 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Development got dropped as a tautology, so a cramped Bd7 that costs 42cp of engine juice is just 'strongest.' The bishop blocks the queen and looks Hippo-passive. If you are going to call a weird developing move best, tell me what it prepares — queenside castle, c6, not silence.

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to g4 is playable, but moving your pawn to c5 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: c5 is a break, not a snack. d4 is covered by Be3, Nf3, and the queen. 'Likely take a pawn' is a PV capture two plies later sold as a free pawn. I would play c5 expecting to win material and then get confused when White just recaptures.

flags.quote: Moving your e3-bishop to g1 is the strongest move because it saves your g1-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The piece that was hanging is the e3-bishop. After the retreat you start calling it the g1-bishop, as if a different piece got saved. Ng4 was attacking e3; I tucked it away. Name the piece by where it was, or say 'this bishop.' Destination-square names make me hunt a ghost.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your d-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and it unveils an attack from your queen on the black pawn.
flags.critique: e5 is defended by d6 and by the knight on g4. This is a central exchange, not picking up a loose pawn. The queen discovery on the d-file is real once the pawn leaves d4 — lead with that if you must — but 'undefended' is a lie. Duplicate discovered_attack in the dump is the smell.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f5 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to h3 would be better.
flags.critique: 130cp, Lichess Mistake, and I still don't know why. h3 kicks the knight that has been sitting on g4 since ply 12. f5 is a pawn lunge that never asks that knight to move. 'That was shaky' plus a SAN is a Stockfish whisper, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your e7-bishop to h4 is a blunder because it forces the king to respond. A better move would have been moving your d7-bishop to c6 because it unveils an attack from your queen on the white queen.
flags.critique: You called a 441cp blunder a blunder because it checks. Checks are not the crime. Nxh4 takes the bishop, and the recapture walks into the queen hitting g4. Concept 'check' made you praise the check as the because-clause on a piece-losing move. I now think checking is how you blunder.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g3 is a blunder, but taking the bishop on h4 with your f3-knight would be better because it unveils an attack from your queen on the black g4-knight.
flags.critique: Take the bishop that just checked you. That is the whole sentence. The discovered queen hit on Ng4 is a bonus after Nf3 leaves the d1–g4 diagonal. You ranked a side discovery over winning a piece, so I might play Nxh4 'to unveil an attack' and miss that g3 just declined a free-ish bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your h4-bishop to e7 is the strongest move because it saves your e7-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Same destination-name bug as Bg1. The bishop is on h4, g3 attacks it, it runs back to e7. 'Saves your e7-bishop' sounds like a different bishop I forgot was hanging. Third time I have to decode square labels to understand 'retreat.'

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: Blank again, on the kick you wanted two plies ago. h3 asks the g4-knight where it lives. Empty reasons, empty because. If the engine finally plays the move you recommended, at least say it chases the knight.

flags.quote: Moving your g4-knight to f6 is the strongest move because it saves your f6-knight from capture.
flags.critique: Third retreat, third destination name. The knight is on g4; h3 is kicking it; it goes to f6. I do not have an f6-knight until after the move. 'It saves the knight from the pawn' is English. This is not.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e5 with your f3-knight is a mistake because the pawn was undefended. A better move would have been moving your queen to d3 because you pin the bishop to the queen.
flags.critique: You told me grabbing an undefended pawn is why the capture is a mistake. That is inverted: wins_material copy on a 127cp error because concept 'capture' still lectures benefits. The pawn being loose is the temptation, not the crime. Qd3 pinning Bd7 to the queen is a real idea — lead with why the grab fails, not with why the grab looks good.

flags.quote: Moving your b8-knight to c6 is a mistake, but moving your e7-bishop to d6 would be better.
flags.critique: Bd6 hits the knight that just ate e5. That is the punishment for ply 23, and you said none of it. Developing Nc6 lets the knight sit. 114cp with an empty because-clause is the same 'shaky' shrug as f5.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on d7 with your e5-knight is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You tagged hanging on a bishop that the queen and king defend. Capture then got dropped as restating the take, so the sentence is a take with no because. This is a knight-for-bishop trade, not a hanging piece. If the lesson is bishop pair, say that.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d7 with your queen is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: White's queen on d1 defends d7. I recaptured a piece that just captured me. wins_material plus 'undefended' on a recapture is the same lie as every equal trade in this dump. Next time you say hanging, I will not believe you.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d7 with your queen is the strongest move because you fork the black king and the black bishop and you take the defender of the black pawn.
flags.critique: I recaptured a queen with check. The queen sitting next to the king also looks at Be7; that is not a fork I get to cash. Black recaptures and the bishop lives. 'Defender of the black pawn' never names which pawn. This is a queen trade, dressed up as two tactics.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on d7 with your f6-knight is the strongest move because the queen was undefended.
flags.critique: I am in check. I recapture. The reason is 'get out of check,' not 'the queen was hanging loot.' King, bishop, and both knights can take on d7. Calling a forced recapture wins_material trains the same false alarm as ply 26.

flags.quote: Moving your d3-bishop to e2 gives the opponent more access to your king. A better move would have been moving your g1-bishop to e3.
flags.critique: The rook just unveiled onto d3. Be2 is a slightly passive tuck of a rook-defended bishop, not a king-safety collapse. back_rank in the tags is leftover panic. If Be3 is better, tell me it develops the idle bishop while d3 stays protected — not that I opened my king.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-knight to d4 puts it where the white d1-rook and g1-bishop can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been taking the rook on d1 with your d8-rook because you fork the white king and the white g1-bishop and then pin the bishop to the rook.
flags.critique: The hanging sentence is the best line in the game: two attackers, you lose a knight. Then the alternative invents a royal fork and a pin. Rxd1+ is a rook check/trade on the first rank. White recaptures; I do not pocket Bg1. Don't garnish a clean hanging-piece lesson with PV fan fiction.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on d4 with your g1-bishop is the strongest move because the knight was undefended.
flags.critique: You just said the rook and bishop can both take it. Rd8 still defends d4. This is 2 vs 1, not undefended. Last ply taught the double attack; this ply unteaches it with the 'undefended' sticker.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on e5 with your d4-bishop is the strongest move because it unveils an attack from your rook on the black d8-rook.
flags.critique: You take a knight. The discovered rook on the d-file is the follow-up you play two moves later. Ranking discovery (145) over winning the piece is the same inverted headline as Nxh4. Lead with the capture; mention the unveiled rook as 'and the d-file opens.'

flags.quote: Taking the rook on d8 with your d1-rook is the strongest move because you fork the black king and the black h8-rook and you take the defender of the black h8-rook.
flags.critique: Same fake-fork template as Qxd7+. A rook recapture with check looks at king and the other rook on the eighth. Black recaptures Rxd8 and nobody wins a second rook. You are already a piece up; this is simplification, not a fork puzzle.

flags.quote: Moving your rook to d1 is the strongest move because it gives your rook an open file.
flags.critique: The d-file was already open. I am offering a rook trade while a piece up. That is the endgame rule I can reuse. 'Open file' is the geometry, not the plan.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on d1 with your rook is the strongest move because it gives your king better protection and it puts the opponent in check.
flags.critique: I recapture a rook with check. king_safer is a stretch: I just traded my last rook. The check is real; 'better protection' is phrase-bank noise glued on because the king is slightly less attacked after the trade. Call it a recapture with check and stop.

suggestions.title: Never praise check or capture on a mistake
suggestions.detail: chooseConcept ranks check/capture above missed_improvement, and explainPlayedAsBenefit then feeds playedBenefits into the because-clause. Bh4+ became 'blunder because it forces the king to respond'; Nxe5 became 'mistake because the pawn was undefended.' If classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, force the problem path (hanging, ignored threat, refutation) and keep check/capture for the suggested move. A 1200 will otherwise learn that checking is how you blunder.

suggestions.title: Stop calling recaptures undefended wins
suggestions.detail: wins_material fires at capturedSeeCp >= 80, then copy says 'the X was undefended' when SEE is near piece value. dxe5 (defended by d6/Ng4), Qxd7 (defended by Qd1), Nxd7 out of check, fxe5 all got that lie. Suppress wins_material when the captured unit arrived last ply, or when defenders exist and SEE is only an exchange. Same detector bug as other games; this dump makes the cry-wolf cost obvious on the later hanging knight.

suggestions.title: Name retreated pieces from the square they left
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses movedPiece on move.to, so Bg1/Be7/Nf6 read as 'saves your g1-bishop / e7-bishop / f6-knight.' Label the saved unit with move.from (or drop the square when only one such piece exists). Cheap NamedUnit fix in pickBenefitReasons; huge eye-roll reduction every time a piece runs away.

suggestions.title: Do not call recapture-with-check a fork
suggestions.detail: detectForks treats king + any other attacked unit as notable. Qxd7+ 'forks king and bishop,' Rxd1+ 'forks king and bishop,' Rxd8+ 'forks king and rook' — all pieces you never win because the forker is recaptured. Suppress fork when the forking piece is hanging by SEE, or when the move is a recapture of a checking/capturing piece. Keep real knight forks.

suggestions.title: Rank taking a piece above discovered-attack flavor
suggestions.detail: discovered_attack severity 145 beats a modest wins_material, and dropTautologyReasons strips the capture, so Nxh4 and Bxe5 advertised unveiled queens/rooks instead of 'take the piece.' When the suggested or best move captures, require capture/wins_material in the because even if discovery is also true. Concatenate: take the bishop, and the queen then hits g4.

suggestions.title: Never emit a better-move SAN with an empty why
suggestions.detail: f5→h3, Nc6→Bd6, and the blank h3 best-move all skipped the idea. skipSuggestionLecture should not apply once evalLoss is in inaccuracy range, and a best pawn kick should still get a because. Name it: h3 kicks Ng4; Bd6 attacks the knight on e5. select-insight already has suggestedBenefits — do not render the SAN without describeBecause.

suggestions.title: Do not sell PV pawn takes as a free pawn
suggestions.detail: c5 vs Ng4 used a likely capture from lineEvents ('you can likely take a pawn') while d4 had three defenders. verifyLikelyTactics already exists; require immediate SEE on the suggested move (or a capture next ply that wins by SEE) before emitting likely capture. Pawn breaks should get a pawn_break / challenges_center reason instead of loot language.

suggestions.title: Add a kicks-piece benefit for pawn attacks
suggestions.detail: h3 vs Ng4 was empty; f5's better move was h3 with no why. kicked_by_pawn is only a problem for the side being chased. Add kicks_piece when a pawn move newly attacks an opponent piece, rank it above center_control, and copy 'it chases the knight.' Reuses namedAttackers / move-effects without an LLM.

whatWorked: Nc3 (ply 11) correctly says it saves the e4 pawn from Nf6 — a real hanging-pawn lesson.
Nde5 (ply 32) names the discovered rook hit on Bd3. That is actual tactics copy.
Nd4's problem sentence (ply 36) names both attackers and 'you lose a knight' before the alternative goes off the rails.
Queenside castling (plies 30–31) at least mentions king shelter and the open d-file.
e5 (ply 14) admits the pawn is at risk, even if 'knight and pawn' undersells four attackers.
